title: HOW TO SURVIVE… · #02

lines.text: Here's how to survive a falling elevator.
Benny's on floor twenty. Then: snap.
First, the good news: this almost never happens.
Elevators hang from several steel cables, and each one could hold the car alone.
If they all fail, safety brakes clamp onto the rails.
That trick was invented in the 1850s. It still works today.
lines.say: That trick was invented in the eighteen fifties. It still works today.

lines.text: But say the brakes fail too. Should Benny jump at the last second?
Nope. Even a perfect jump barely slows you down.
And standing? Your legs take the whole hit.
Best move: lie flat on your back and cover your head.
That spreads the impact across your whole body.
In 1945, one woman survived a 75-floor elevator fall.
lines.say: In nineteen forty-five, one woman survived a seventy-five floor elevator fall.

sources: Live Science / NBC: lie flat on your back, cover your head; jumping is a myth
ScienceABC: an Olympic-level jump removes only ~4 m/s from ~30 m/s; modern elevators have multiple safety brakes, true free fall is rare
Sciencefocus: brakes clamp onto the shaft rails if cables fail
Guinness: Betty Lou Oliver survived a 75-storey elevator fall, Empire State Building, 1945
